title: How Effectively Do Security Skills Guide Coding Agents in Vulnerability Detection in Linux Kernel?
title_zh: 安全技能能在多大程度上有效指导编码智能体进行 Linux 内核漏洞检测？

paragraphs.en: 总结：研究首次大规模实证评估安全技能引导编程智能体检测Linux内核漏洞的效果，并提出自进化框架SKILL-SIF显著提升检出率。 Large language model (LLM) coding agents, such as Claude Code, are increasingly used for security auditing, with task-specific skills providing reusable vulnerability-analysis procedures. However, their effectiveness in detecting real vulnerabilities and the reasons for their failures remain unclear. We conduct the first large-scale empirical study of 37 security skills using Claude Code with four underlying LLMs on 100 real Linux kernel vulnerabilities across ten classes, totaling 14800 runs. We evaluate vulnerability detection at the function, statement, and vulnerability-class levels. Results show that 24.4 percent of runs locate the correct function, 18.3 percent identify both the function and responsible statement, and 15.7 percent correctly classify the vulnerability. Our failure analysis reveals limitations in evidence acquisition, state-relation reasoning, code interpretation, candidate verification, investigation coverage, and reporting. Based on these findings, we propose SKILL-SIF, a self-improving framework that iteratively evolves security skills by learning from missed vulnerabilities and failure patterns. We evolve five top-performing skills using the original benchmark and evaluate them on 100 previously unseen vulnerabilities. SKILL-SIF improves fully correct vulnerability detection by up to eight times (from 2 percent to 16 percent) on unseen vulnerabilities, while aggregate accuracy across four LLMs increases by 1.85 times (from 6.05 percent to 11.20 percent). These findings highlight the limitations of existing security skills and demonstrate the potential of failure-driven skill evolution to improve vulnerability detection in coding agents.
paragraphs.zh: 总结：研究首次大规模实证评估安全技能引导编程智能体检测Linux内核漏洞的效果，并提出自进化框架SKILL-SIF显著提升检出率。 Claude Code等大语言模型（LLM）编程智能体正被越来越多地用于安全审计，任务专用技能提供了可复用的漏洞分析流程。 然而，它们在检测真实漏洞方面的有效性及其失败的原因仍不明确。 我们使用Claude Code和四种底层LLM，针对十类共100个真实Linux内核漏洞，对37个安全技能开展了首次大规模实证研究，共计14800次运行。 我们在函数、语句和漏洞类别三个层面评估漏洞检测效果。 结果显示，24.4%的运行定位到正确的函数，18.3%同时识别出函数和责任语句，15.7%正确分类了漏洞。 我们的失败分析揭示了在证据获取、状态关系推理、代码解读、候选验证、调查覆盖面和报告方面的局限。 基于这些发现，我们提出SKILL-SIF，这是一个自改进框架，通过从漏检漏洞和失败模式中学习来迭代演化安全技能。 我们使用原始基准对五个表现最佳的技能进行演化，并在100个此前未见过的漏洞上进行评估。 在未见过的漏洞上，SKILL-SIF将完全正确的漏洞检测提升至多八倍（从2%到16%），同时四个LLM的总体准确率提升1.85倍（从6.05%到11.20%）。 这些发现凸显了现有安全技能的局限性，并展示了失败驱动的技能演化在提升编程智能体漏洞检测能力方面的潜力。
